claims.text: Security/authz: every new entry point (/sign, /api/sign, /preview, /api/preview) refuses a missing or wrong token, a foreign Origin or a foreign Host with 403 and a GET with 405, writing nothing and logging nothing.

Security/input: the snapshot must match 64 hex characters (no path traversal into packs/), the name is normalised and capped at 200 characters, the name is shown escaped in HTML, and unknown body fields are refused with 400 (test_r23_a_snapshot_no_preview_recorded_is_refused, test_r22_a_sign_off_needs_a_typed_name, test_workspace_preview_page_offers_the_sign_off_form_and_escapes_the_text, test_workspace_sign_off_refuses_a_stale_preview_naming_what_changed).
Security/deps and secrets: no new dependency, no secret; ruff and compileall clean.
claims.proof_cmd: ruff check src tests; python -m compileall -q src && echo compile-ok

claims.text: Failure modes/idempotency: a second sign-off of the same snapshot is refused and the pack is never overwritten; a folder already at the snapshot's path is never replaced.

Failure modes/partial failure: a crash at the rename leaves no visible pack and nothing logged, leftover .part folders are removed on the next start, and a log refusal of the pack-written entry removes the pack; the CLI reports a save not recorded as exit 4 with no pack. Gap: a failure of the second (signed_off) append is not repairable (see notes).
Failure modes: a broken or incomplete case log is refused naming the first bad entry from the CLI (exit 3) and from the workspace (409 with first_bad), writing nothing.
Failure modes/external calls: not applicable. Sign-off makes no network or model call; the pack is built from the figures layer, and its evidence records egress offline.

Data/migrations: additive only (new packs/<snapshot> folders and new case-log event kinds pack_written and signed_off); no stored format changes; owner-only modes on the pack folder and files; every Tier 1 event kind is present in a signed case's log, which verifies intact.

Data/stale snapshot: a change to the override log, the profile, a statement, an added account, the field map or show_policy_verdict is refused naming what changed, with the case folder byte-identical and the log unchanged.
Performance: not a hot path. One sign-off rebuilds the figures once while holding the case; no query or list endpoint is added.

Observability: the behaviour is proven by case-log entries pack_written (snapshot, pack path, file hashes) and signed_off (name, OS user, UTC time, snapshot, file hashes); no remote alerting by design (design: Observability), and refusals exit non-zero.
claims.proof_output: 32 passed (test_sign_off_writes_memo_and_evidence_once_bound_to_the_snapshot asserts entries[-3:] == preview, pack_written, signed_off with hashes)

claims.text: Operability/rollback: new command and new routes only; packs are immutable; an older package ignores packs/ and the unknown log events; reinstalling the previous wheel is the rollback. No config or secret change for deploy.
claims.proof_output: src/cma/cli.py, src/cma/pack.py, src/cma/review/server.py, src/cma/review/signoff.py (new), src/cma/review/summary.py: additive

claims.text: No regression: the full suite passes with the hardening tests.
Docs: README documents cma case sign and the workspace sign-off; the design already covers C6 and the case-log events, so no ADR change is needed.
claims.proof_output: README.md: 'cma case sign <id>' with refusal and exit-code text

notes: Gaps for the owner: (1) Partial failure not repairable: if the pack_written entry is recorded and the signed_off append then fails (SaveNotRecorded), the pack and pack_written stay with no signed_off entry, and every retry is refused as 'already signed off' (sign_off checks packs/<snapshot>.exists()). It needs a design choice: one combined entry, or a retry that appends only signed_off when pack_written's hashes match the folder. (2) signoff._refusal does not map PolicyError, ThresholdsError, RulesetError, AmountError or StatementError; in the workspace these become a generic 500 'could not be saved' rather than the named refusal the CLI gives. (3) server._origin_ok accepts a request with no Origin header (all([]) is True); the token and Host still guard. This was already true for /override before T27, and the design says writes carry the workspace's Origin. (4) packs/ itself being a symlink is followed by mkdir and rename; leftover cleanup skips symlinked children only. No new dependency or service was needed.
